chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqteen who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the sale of the mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon the owner's death). He said: 'If the owner gave permission for it, there is no harm in it. And if there was a debt upon the master of the slave, and he manumitted him to escape the debt, there is no manumission for him. And if he manumitted him while in health and soundness, the creditor has no claim against him, and his manumission proceeds.'

key_terms.بَيْعِ الْمُدَبَّرِ: Sale of the mudabbir (slave manumitted upon death)
key_terms.فَلاَ تَدْبِيرَ لَهُ: There is no manumission for him (voided)
key_terms.فَلاَ سَبِيلَ لِلدُّيَّانِ عَلَيْهِ: The creditor has no claim against him
key_terms.فِي صِحَّةٍ وَ سَلاَمَةٍ: In health and soundness (free from illness)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a mudabbir slave if the owner has debts?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the jurisprudential distinction between a valid sale of a *mudabbir* and one executed as a fraudulent conveyance to evade creditors. It highlights the Shia legal principle that manumission remains binding if the owner was in good health when authorizing the sale, thereby protecting the slave’s right to freedom from debt claims.
